saints.name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The bishop of Jerusalem whose Lenten “Catechetical Lectures” still teach the faith to those preparing for baptism…
biography: Born about 315 at or near Jerusalem, Cyril was ordained deacon by Bishop Macarius about 335 and priest by Maximus some eight years later, and about the year 350 he succeeded Maximus as bishop of the holy city of his birth.

His episcopate fell in the heat of the Arian controversy. Accused by Acacius of Caesarea of selling church treasures — sacred vessels he had sold, the historians say, to feed the starving — he was deposed in 357 and driven three times into exile under the emperors Constantius and Valens, returning for good in 378.

His fame rests on his Catechetical Lectures, eighteen instructions to candidates for baptism with five mystagogical lectures on the sacraments, preached in Constantine's basilica and still a chief witness to the creed and liturgy of the fourth-century Church. Present at the First Council of Constantinople in 381, he died in 386 and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1883.
saints.knownFor: His Catechetical Lectures and his defense of orthodoxy.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; declared Doctor of the Church 1883 by Pope Leo XIII

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 18 March
